Shri Venkatesh Bharath Gangadharan Ashutosh Kumar Srivastava Nihal Bhardwaj Siddharth Nigotia Shivam Kumar Kartikay Trivedi Aashwyn Singh Punyam Bhutani _1._ Two separate but identical tariff orders dated 01.03.2019 passed by 1[st] respondent West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as the Commission) for the years 2014-15 and 2015-16 in respect of the appellant Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) have been assailed in these two appeals. Vide the said impugned orders, the Commission has held that sale of power by DVC to West Bengal State Electricity Distribution ______________________________________________________________________________ Appeal Nos.190 & 216 of 2019 Page 4 of 22_ 5. In this backdrop, both WBSEDCL and IPCL approached the Commission with two separate petitions on 11.07.2018 and 25.04.2018 numbered OA No.273/18-19 and OA No.272/18-19 respectively praying for a direction to DVC not to impose retail tariff determined for the consumers of DVC in tariff order dated 25.05.2015 on the bulk sale of power to WBSEDCL ______________________________________________________________________________ Appeal Nos.190 & 216 of 2019 Page 5 of 22_ 6. These two petitions have been disposed of by the Commission vide the two identical but separate orders dated 01.03.2019 which have been impugned in these two appeals. 7. The contention of the appellant is that impugned orders are vitiated by error of law and jurisdiction in as much as the Commission has proceeded on legally unsustainable assumptions and has given contradictory findings. It is pointed out that: - - (c) the Commission has wrongfully refused to adjudicate the tariff applicable to an admitted quantum of supply and has, by relegating the parties to settle the matter mutually, abdicated its statutory function under Section 86(1)(b) of the Act; - (d) the impugned orders disregarded Commission’s own prior findings in the tariff proceedings initiated in the tariff proceedings in respect of WBSDCL and IPCL where it expressly treated DVC’s radial supply as a component of power purchase cost of these two entities thereby accepting radial supply as a legitimate and regulated category. 10. The appellant further contends that the impugned orders have left it without any lawful mechanism to recover the under recovered tariff from WBSEDCL and IPCL. 11. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant DVC, learned counsels appearing for the WBSEDCL and IPCL as well as the learned counsel appearing for the Commission. ______________________________________________________________________________ Appeal Nos.190 & 216 of 2019 Page 9 of 22_ 17. In this regard we may profitability refer to the following observations of this Tribunal in K. Raheja Corporation Private Limited v. MERC and Anr. (2011) SCC online APTEL 105:- 18. Similarly, in a recent judgement in West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited v. Considering these factual aspects as well as the law laid down by this Tribunal in the above noted previous judgements, we are unable to accept the contention on behalf of the DVC that supply of power by it to WBSEDCL and IPCL on radial mode ought to be treated as sale of power by a generating company to a consumer. 23. We also note that in the recent judgement dated 15.09.2025 passed in appeal number 275 of 2015 and batch DVPCA v. WBERC & Ors. 2025 SCC OnLine APTEL 65, this tribunal has held as under: - ## _not the actual revenue realized) in the subject APR petition that was filed much later on 06.09.2020._ _**”**_ 24. In the backdrop of observations in these two Paragraphs of the judgement, this tribunal directed DVC to refund the excess amount recovered by it from its consumers which were attributable to erroneous billing to WBSEDCL and IPCL for power supplied at the retail supply tariff and consequent erroneous accounting. We have been informed by learned counsel for WBSEDCL and IPCL that the said judgement has been challenged by DVC in the Hon’ble Supreme Court and while directing that the judgement shall not be given effect to, the Supreme Court clarified that the proceeding before the West Bengal Commission in terms of the said judgement of this Tribunal has not been stayed. and known as WBERC (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2021, the relevant portion of which are quoted hereinbelow: - ______________________________________________________________________________ Appeal Nos.190 & 216 of 2019 Page 18 of 22_ at various offtake points. At that time DVC exercised monopoly in supply of electricity and thus billed these two entities also at retail tariff. This arrangement continued between the parties even after the passing of the Electricity Act, 2003 till the year 2015 when the tariff orders dated 04.03.2015 and 25.05.2015 came to be issued by the Commission for WBSEDCL and IPCL respectively wherein the principles of 2003 Act were applied. Therefore, DVC cannot be heard to take advantage of the arrangements between the parties that had commenced prior to the passing of 2003 Act for the reason that subsequent to passing of the 2003 Act, the transactions between the parties have to be governed strictly by the provisions of the said Act. 29. Hence, considering the above discussion, the two issues formulated by us in Paragraph No.12 of this judgment stand answered in negative.
title: Damodar Valley Corporation VERSUS West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission & Anr
